translationRepairs: Promoted to judicial investigator at Yanping and then appointed investigating censor on the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, he impeached Dashi Timur, left chancellor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, for betraying the state. Invoking the Han precedent of Emperor Gaozu executing Lord Ding, he argued to make plain the supreme duty owed by a subject to his sovereign.

Transferred to assistant prefect of Yanping and then appointed investigating censor on the Shaanxi Branch Censorate, he impeached Dashi Timur, left chancellor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, for betraying the state. Invoking the Han precedent of Emperor Gaozu executing Lord Ding, he argued to make plain the supreme duty owed by a subject to his sovereign.
轉 is a lateral transfer, 判官 is the assistant-prefect (panguan) post, and 陝西行臺 is the Shaanxi Branch Censorate, not a branch secretariat.

Recalled to serve again as investigating censor, Liangzhen judged that with the emperor now personally attending to the myriad affairs of government, he could not afford to neglect recruiting worthy advisers. He therefore submitted a series of memorials: "During the Tianshun era the laws and institutions fell into grave disorder and the vital energies of the dynasty were grievously depleted.

Recalled to serve again as investigating censor, Liangzhen judged that with the emperor now personally attending to the myriad affairs of government, he could not afford to neglect recruiting worthy advisers. He therefore submitted a series of memorials: "During the Tianli years the laws and institutions fell into grave disorder and the vital energies of the dynasty were grievously depleted.
天曆 is the Yuan Tianli era (1328–1330). Tianshun names the later Ming era 天順 and is a false reading.

He also said that by national custom, when the father dies one marries his father's younger brother's wife; when a brother dies one takes his brother's wife; when parents die there is no mourning observance—thereupon he said: "The constants of human relations all come from Heaven and cannot be changed; yet the officials who deliberate on law say that Mongols are not bound by this rule and that people of the various states each follow their native customs.

He also said that by national custom, when the father dies one marries his stepmother; when a brother dies one takes his brother's wife; when parents die there is no mourning observance—thereupon he said: "The constants of human relations all come from Heaven and cannot be changed; yet the officials who deliberate on law say that Mongols are not bound by this rule and that people of the various states each follow their native customs.
妻其從母 is levirate marriage of the father's other wife (stepmother), not the wife of a father's younger brother. The rest of the literal sentence is unchanged and sound.

When a eunuch named Han, having lost a favored concubine, killed his wife, minced her flesh, and fed it to his dogs, Liangzhen memorialized asking that the severest penalty be imposed. He also argued that eunuchs who colluded with court officials to obstruct government were a grave evil and ought to be purged.

When the eunuch Hanshi's favored concubine killed his wife, minced her flesh, and fed it to dogs, Liangzhen memorialized asking that the severest penalty be imposed. He also argued that eunuchs who colluded with court officials to obstruct government were a grave evil and ought to be purged.
宦者罕失 is the eunuch's name Hanshi; 嬖妾殺其妻 makes the favored concubine the killer. The original wrongly split 失 as the verb 'lost' and made Hanshi the murderer.

龔伯璲 is Gong Bosui: 璲 is suì, not juǎn. The rest of the idiomatic sentence is unchanged.

Earlier, the Taizhou bandit Zhang Shicheng had submitted and then rebelled again, killing Participant in Government Zhao Lian of the Huainan Branch Secretariat and advancing to occupy Gaoyou and Luhe; Grand Preceptor Toghto received the edict and commanded the armies of the imperial princes on a southern campaign, and Liangzhen together with Participant Gong Bosui, director of affairs Lu Shan of the Ministry of Punishments, and others followed him.
The same given-name error appears in the literal field: 伯璲 is Bosui, not Bojuan.

He once argued that the Zhizheng code's gradations of punishment were inconsistent, allowing clerks to exploit the gaps for fraud. He nominated several experts in the Ming code to consult past and present precedents and redraft the statutes. The new code was completed, but the project was abandoned.

He once argued that the Zhizheng code's gradations of punishment were inconsistent, allowing clerks to exploit the gaps for fraud. He nominated several experts well versed in the statutes to consult past and present precedents and redraft the law book. The new code was completed, but the project was abandoned.
舉明律者數人 means he nominated men who understood the statutes clearly. A 'Ming code' is anachronistic in a Zhizheng (Yuan) setting.

He once argued that the Zhizheng code's gradations of severity were inconsistent, allowing clerks to exploit both and commit fraud; he nominated several who understood the Ming code, consulted past and present, and redrafted the law book—the book was completed but the project was abandoned.

He once argued that the Zhizheng code's gradations of severity were inconsistent, allowing clerks to exploit both and commit fraud; he nominated several who understood the statutes clearly, consulted past and present, and redrafted the law book—the book was completed but the project was abandoned.
In the literal field likewise, 明律 is the verb-object 'understand the statutes,' not the Ming-dynasty code.

In 1352 Grand Tutor and Right Chancellor Toghto returned to power. When the river breach was discussed, wishing to relieve the people's suffering and fulfill the imperial mandate, he convened the court for collective deliberation—but every minister had a different opinion.

In 1349 Grand Tutor and Right Chancellor Toghto returned to power. When the river breach was discussed, wishing to relieve the people's suffering and fulfill the imperial mandate, he convened the court for collective deliberation—but every minister had a different opinion.
九年 in this Zhizheng biography is 1349. Rendering it 1352 contradicts both the Chinese year-count and the following eleventh-year (1351) river campaign.

The emperor was just then reading memorials from censorate officials commending Toghto's achievements in controlling the river. Jia Lu's merits were discussed next. He was specially promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Academician-Expositor of the Hall for Advancing Worthies, rewarded with gold and silks, and ordered that Academician-Recipient Ouyang Xuan of the Hanlin Academy compose a stele commemorating the pacification of the river—honoring Toghto's labors while fully recording Jia Lu's achievements. The text was ordered proclaimed and deposited in the History Office, and honors were extended to three generations of Jia Lu's forebears.

The emperor was just then reading memorials from censorate officials commending Toghto's achievements in controlling the river. Jia Lu's merits were discussed next. He was specially promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Academician of the Hall of Worthies, rewarded with gold and silks, and ordered that Academician-Recipient Ouyang Xuan of the Hanlin Academy compose a stele commemorating the pacification of the river—honoring Toghto's labors while fully recording Jia Lu's achievements. 集賢大學士 is Grand Academician of the Hall of Worthies (Jixian), not Academician-Expositor (侍講學士).

Soon afterward he was appointed left vice grand councillor and accompanied Toghto in pacifying Xuzhou. After Toghto withdrew his army, Jia Lu was ordered to pursue remnant rebels and divide his forces to attack Haozhou. Pingzhang Yexekä'r, serving as overall military commander, joined him in supervising the campaign. Jia Lu addressed the troops: "By imperial order I command the eight Han guard units. 緫兵官平章月可察兒督戰 names him pingzhang and overall commander who jointly supervised the fighting. Pacification Commissioner renders 宣慰使, which is not in the sentence.
He replied: "Empress Zhenge in Emperor Wuzong's reign already received the jade register, and thus was Empress of Wuzong; the two empresses of Mingzong and Wenzong were by nature concubines.
He replied: "Empress Zhenge in Emperor Wuzong's reign already received the jade register, and thus was Empress of Wuzong; the two mothers of Mingzong and Wenzong were by nature concubines.
明宗、文宗二母后 are the two mothers of Mingzong and Wenzong, matching Bayan's preceding question (明宗母 / 文宗母), not empresses belonging to those two reigns.

Academician-Expositor Chen Hao of the Hall for Advancing Worthies, who had long resented Luceng, objected: "Emperor Taizong of Tang ennobled the mother of Prince Cao as empress—were there not then two empresses? Why should this not be permitted?"

Grand Academician Chen Hao of the Hall for Advancing Worthies, who had long resented Luceng, objected: "Emperor Taizong of Tang enregistered the mother of Prince Cao Ming as empress—were there not then two empresses? Why should this not be permitted?"
集賢大學士 is Grand Academician; 冊 is enregistering by patent, not a generic ennoblement; and 曹王明 includes the given name Ming omitted in the original.

Reappointed investigating censor, he impeached Grand Guardian Dashihaiya, Grand Guardian Ajila, Right Vice Councillor Gongbuban, Minister of Punishments Utuman, Investigating Censor Jidangpu, Court Commissioners Harqanju and Yuelubuhua, and Director Lü Sicheng. All were dismissed.
月魯不花 is the Mongol personal name Yuelubuhua, not the Khitan surname 耶律 (Yelü) plus Buhua.

In 1352 Chancellor Toghto campaigned against the Xuzhou rebels. Because government troops were unaccustomed to the local climate, he recruited coastal salt workers as soldiers. Luceng was specially promoted to Grand Master for the Good of the Heir Apparent and pacification commissioner of Huainan, placed in charge of the punitive campaign, and five thousand salt workers he recruited were sent with the army.

In 1352 Chancellor Toghto campaigned against the Xuzhou rebels. Because government troops were unaccustomed to the local climate, he recruited coastal salt workers as soldiers. Luceng was specially promoted to Grand Master of Assisting Virtue and pacification commissioner of Huainan, placed in charge of the punitive campaign, and five thousand salt workers he recruited were sent with the army.
資善大夫 is the prestige title Grand Master of Assisting Virtue. The original invents an office of the Heir Apparent that the Chinese does not state.

Shitai made secret inquiries and learned that a villager named Shen Ding, returning from carrying goods to Hangzhou, had cast nets in the sea and was killed by fishermen when he stole fish from their nets. Shi had never killed anyone or seized goods, and Gao knew nothing of the affair. The innocence of both men was established.

Shitai made secret inquiries and learned that a villager named Shen Ding, returning from carrying goods to Hangzhou, stole fish from nets fishermen had cast in the sea and was killed by those fishermen. Shi had never killed anyone or seized goods, and Gao knew nothing of the affair. The innocence of both men was established.
漁者張網海中 makes the fishermen the net-casters; Shen Ding stole from those nets and was killed. The original wrongly has Shen Ding casting the nets.

Shitai secretly inquired and learned that Shen Ding of the village, carrying goods to Hangzhou and returning, had cast nets in the sea; because he stole fish from the nets he was killed by the fishermen; Shi in truth had never killed men or seized goods, and Gao also did not know— their wrongful guilt was all cleared.

Shitai secretly inquired and learned that Shen Ding of the village, carrying goods to Hangzhou and returning, stole fish from nets that fishermen had spread in the sea and was killed by the fishermen; Shi in truth had never killed men or seized goods, and Gao also did not know—their wrongful guilt was all cleared.
The literal field has the same agent error: the subject of 張網 is 漁者, not Shen Ding.

His father Yingji, during the Zhida period when Renzong was crown prince, was summoned to audience and presented an Ode to the Primal Origin of the Sovereign. Renzong spoke of him to Wuzong, and he was appointed Hanlin attendant.
After the crown prince summoned Yingji and received the ode, 為言于武宗 is Renzong speaking to Wuzong on Yingji's behalf, not Yingji talking to Wuzong about the poem.
